UI.Saved: The journey is written in slot %1.
UI.GameOver: The last lamp gutters out. The fog closes over the road...
UI.BattleAppear: Shapes rise out of the fog!
UI.BattleEscaped: The party slips away into the fog.
UI.BattleCannotRun: There is no running from this one.
UI.LampLit: The lamp burns steady. The fog beside it is firm.
UI.LampLocked: The wick is too short to light from here.
UI.LampLights: Pell touches his flame to the wick. The fog around the post hardens with a soft creak.
UI.LampEastLocked: A post of the East Lanterway. Only the Lamp House may light it.
UI.LampSouthLocked: A post of the South Lanterway, sealed by the Lamp Office.
UI.LampTideLocked: The harbour post is capped. The Council keeps the Tide road dark.
UI.LampSpurLocked: The last post of the Spur. Its wick has been cut.
UI.BellpostRing: An old bell post. Pell rings it, and the fog below listens.
UI.TravelAsk: Where should the fog carry the party?
UI.SmithHello: Blades, poles and pans. Something for everyone.
UI.TailorHello: Good cloth turns more than weather.
UI.MothShopHello: We trade in things the fog let fall. Look gently.
UI.InnAsk: A bed and a hot meal for %1 glints?
UI.InnMorning: Good morning! The road's waiting for you.
UI.InnPoor: Ah. Come back when your purse is heavier.
UI.BedAsk: Pell's bed. Rest a while to get your HP and WICK back?
UI.BedDone: Pell wakes rested. Everyone feels better.
UI.WennaAsk: Rest by the moth fire for a while?
UI.WennaMorning: The moths kept watch. Go well.
UI.WennaBye: The fire will wait for you.
UI.SignInnBed: Clean sheets and a pillow that smells of lavender.
UI.Chapter6Sub: The Old Man of the Roads
UI.Intro1: The Murk: a sea of fog with no shore. Only the holds rise above it, and the lamplit roads that join them.
UI.Intro2: Where a lamp burns, the fog holds firm underfoot. Where a lamp fails, the fog gives way, and whatever stood on it is gone.
UI.Intro3: PELL! Up! Your trial is this morning and your boots are on the roof again!
UI.Intro4: ...The roof? How do they keep getting onto the roof?
UI.Intro5: You walked in your sleep and tried to light the weathervane. Twice.
UI.Intro6: It looked very dark up there.
UI.Intro7: Boots by the door, I fetched them. Old Hesk is waiting at the Lamp House. Go, and come back a wickwarden!
UI.MartaTalk1: Hesk won't wait. He's been lighting lamps since before the fog had a name.
UI.MartaTalk2: Bring me back a jar of candlenut honey. And both of your boots.
UI.MartaTalk3: Supper's at dusk. Hesk is doing the dishes. For six years.
UI.MartaRest: Tired out? Your bed's right there. A good sleep brings back your HP and your WICK.
UI.SpurNotYet: I should see master Hesk at the Lamp House first.
UI.SignPellShelf: Pell's shelf: three wick trimmers, one sock, a drawing of a lamp signed 'age 6'.
UI.SignLampMachine: The great wick press of the Lamp House. It smells of oil and old summers.
UI.SignLampShelf: Rows of brass caps, oil cans and spare wicks, each labelled in Hesk's tiny hand.
UI.SignTallowby: TALLOWBY. East: the Old Spur. Southeast: the East Lanterway.
UI.HeskTalk0: Let the boy sleep, Marta. He'll need it.
UI.Trial1: Pell. Late as the moon. Good. A wickwarden who hurries trips over his own pole.
UI.Trial2: Sorry, master Hesk. My boots were...
UI.Trial3: On the roof. All of Tallowby saw. Never mind. Your trial: the Old Spur, east of the village.
UI.Trial4: Three posts out there went dark last night. Relight them all and you walk home a wickwarden.
UI.Trial5: Take this wickpole. Touch its flame to a dark post, and the fog beside it will hold your weight.
UI.Trial6: And if something out there doesn't want them lit?
UI.Trial7: Then you hit it with the pole. Lamplighting is mostly walking, and a little hitting.
UI.Trial8: Press START to check your gear on the road. Now go.
UI.HeskWait: The Spur is east of the village. Three posts. Off you go.
UI.HeskLast: Three posts, Pell. Not two. The last one is on the islet at the end.
UI.Spur2: Hey! That post belongs to the Lamp House! Put that knife down!
UI.Spur3: Go home, little wick. The roads are going dark, all of them. Better you learn it now.
UI.Spur4: He walked onto the bare fog... and it held him? That's not possible.
UI.Spur5: The fog churns. Something rises out of it!
UI.Spur6: Mistmites. They hate the light... so why do I feel sorry for them?
UI.Spur7: The wick was cut clean through. Pell splices it and lights it again.
UI.Spur8: That's all three. Master Hesk needs to hear about that man.
UI.Report1: All three burning. I saw them from the window. Well done, wickwarden.
UI.Report2: Wickwarden! ...Master, a man was cutting the wicks. Then he walked off across the open fog.
UI.Report3: A Snuffer. They've been seen on the far roads. Walking the bare Murk, you say.
UI.Report4: Fog is fog, boy. It holds no one without light. He must have had some trick.
UI.Report5: Some trick? He didn't even look down.
UI.Report6: Here's your first real errand. Tallowby's oil cart is three days late. Go to Wickhollow, where the glimmer is pressed, and find out why.
UI.Report7: The way east is shut by a Murk Wall. Light the Watchlight on the shore past the Spur; its fire will part it. Take these, and keep your wick dry.
UI.HeskTalk4: Wickhollow is east along the lanterway. Mind the sootcrows; they peck at eyes and lamps alike.
UI.HeskTalk7: Glimmerhold, eh? Keep your head down around the Council, Pell.
UI.TalOld1: Big day for you, lad! I remember my own trial. A mistmite ate my hat.
UI.TalOld2: No oil cart this week. My lamp's on its last finger of glimmer.
UI.TalOld3: Bells on the roads again. Haven't heard that since I had hair.
UI.TalKid1: When I grow up I'm going to be a wickwarden too! Or a frog.
UI.TalKid2: Is it true the fog eats people? My sister says it only nibbles.
UI.TalKid3: I can ring a bell AND light a lamp now. I'm both!
UI.TalMiller1: Hesk's been out late every night this month. That man never sleeps.
UI.TalMiller2: If the oil doesn't come, we'll be eating supper in the dark.
UI.TalMiller3: The roads hum at night now, when the bells ring. It's a lovely sound.
UI.TalSnuffNight: Easy, wickwarden. We're not here to hurt anyone. The Old Man's inside.
UI.TalSnuffNight2: Six years we've been cutting wicks for him. Go on in.
UI.WickFarmer: Snuffers went into the Orchard Caves with all that oil. I'm not going in there. Nobody's going in there.
UI.WickPicker1: The candlenut trees don't care who steals the oil. They just keep growing.
UI.WickPicker2: Every barrel we press goes to Glimmerhold now. 'For the Kindling', they say.
UI.WickPicker3: We're pressing oil for the bell-ringers' lanterns now. Small ones. Polite ones.
UI.WickElder1: Press-house was robbed last night. Poor Bram's beside himself.
UI.WickElder2: Mind the forms at the Lamp Office. Pottle loves his forms.
UI.WickKid1: Bram gave me a burnt biscuit once. It was the best day of my life.
UI.WickKid2: Is it true Bram fought a giant bell? He told us he did. Twice.
UI.SignWickhollow: WICKHOLLOW, where the glimmer is pressed. North: Orchard Caves. South: South Lanterway.
UI.SignPress: The great glimmer press. Candlenuts go in at the top; light comes out of the bottom.
UI.BramBusy: Not now, I'm reducing a sauce. Emotionally.
UI.Presser1: We pressed for three days straight, and the Snuffers took every drop.
UI.Presser2: The barrels are back! Mostly. Some smell of fried onions now.
UI.Bram1: Out! Out of my kitchen! ...Oh. You're not a thief. Thieves don't knock that politely.
UI.Bram2: I'm Pell, from Tallowby. Our oil never came. I was sent to see why.
UI.Bram3: Bram Odge, cook of the press-house. Your oil was in our cellar. Past tense.
UI.Bram4: Snuffers came in the night. They took every barrel of glimmer, the spare wicks... and my good frying pan.
UI.Bram6: Seasoned for nineteen years! You can't buy a pan like that, wickwarden. You can only earn it.
UI.Bram7: Their tracks lead into the Orchard Caves, north of the village. I'm going in after them.
UI.Bram9: Good. I hit things with ladles. You hit things with that stick. We'll be a terror.
UI.Pottle1: Lamp Office, Wickhollow branch. State your business. Preferably in writing.
UI.Pottle2: Stolen oil? Then you need Form 12-B, Report of Stolen Glimmer, in triplicate. We are out of Form 12-B.
UI.Pottle3: Form 12-B has turned up! Forty of them! Nobody needs one any more, of course.
UI.Pottle4: I'm drafting Form 1: Abolition of Form 12-B. It needs a Form 12-B to be filed. I'm working on it.
UI.SignForms: Shelves of forms, sorted by colour, then by mood.
UI.Gorse1: Far enough, wicks. This oil goes home with us to Farrow's Reach.
UI.Gorse3: ...The pan's very good. We've been cooking with it.
UI.Gorse4: You've been COOKING with it?! On what heat?!
UI.Gorse5: Enough... enough. Take your oil. Take your pan.
UI.Gorse6: Why steal it at all? Who are you people?
UI.Gorse7: Farmers. From Farrow's Reach, past the Hollow Roads. Six weeks ago the Lamp Council stopped sending oil out our way.
UI.Gorse8: 'All glimmer goes to the Great Kindling,' they said. Our roads went dark. Folk who walked them... sank.
UI.Gorse9: ...Six weeks without light. Pell, we can't take it all back from them.
UI.Gorse10: Half. The Old Man said there were still good wickwardens left. I didn't believe him.
UI.Gorse11: Then pray your own roads never go dark, wickwarden.
UI.Gorse12: Wait. How do you cross the bare fog? I saw one of you walk on it.
UI.Gorse13: The Old Man taught us. That's all I'll say. Ask the fog, wickwarden. It answers more than you'd think.
UI.Gorse14: My pan! Look at her! Not a scratch. They even oiled her. ...Pell, I think I like those people.
UI.Pass1: You caught the Snuffers? Without Form 12-B? That's highly irregular. Splendid, but irregular.
UI.Pass2: And a notice came from the Council: every wickwarden is summoned to Glimmerhold for the Great Kindling.
UI.Pass3: The way runs through Brassmouth. With Form 12-B you may light the Watchlight of the East Isles; it holds back the wall to the south. Oh, and take this. We found a stack.
UI.Pass4: I'm coming too. Someone has to make sure you eat. And I want to see what this Kindling is cooking.
UI.Meet1: A young woman rounds the corner with an armful of charts, nose deep in one of them...
UI.Meet2: My charts! No, no, don't step on that one, that's the whole eastern current!
UI.Meet3: Sorry! I'm sorry! Here, let me...
UI.Meet4: You're holding it upside down. ...You're a wickwarden. You have soot on your nose.
UI.Meet6: Ottilie Vane, surveyor. I chart the Murk. Not the roads: the fog itself.
UI.Meet7: It moves, did you know? It swells and sinks, slowly, like something breathing.
UI.Meet8: Pell. Pell. She's talking to you. Say something clever.
UI.Meet10: The Tide Lanterway to Glimmerhold went dark. The Council says it can't be relit until after the Kindling.
UI.Meet11: My brother Tobin sank on that road two years ago. I want to see it. I have a chart of the currents that could get us across.
UI.Meet12: You need to reach Glimmerhold. I need an escort who carries a flame. Deal?
UI.Meet13: Good. I'll walk with you, then. Try not to hold anything upside down.
UI.Meet14: One thing first. Old Hobb at the bell tower says the old roads never needed lamps. Everyone says he's mad. I want his opinion anyway.
UI.SignBrassmouth: BRASSMOUTH. Bell tower: north. Harbour and Tide Lanterway: east.
UI.SignStatue: A statue of the first wickwarden. Someone has tied a tiny bell to her wrist.
UI.SignCharts: Charts of currents nobody else has measured, in neat green ink.
UI.SignCharts2: A chart titled 'Where Tobin sank'. Every line on it is drawn very carefully.
UI.Pim1: Miss Vane's out measuring the fog again. She does that every day. Even Sundays.
UI.Pim2: Look after Miss Vane. She acts like she's made of brass, but she's made of paper.
UI.Pim3: Tobin's back and he's already moved all the charts. Miss Vane is furious. And happy. Mostly happy.
UI.BrassSailor1: Tide road's been dark a month. Ships can't sail fog, mate. We're just men standing on a dock.
UI.BrassSailor2: Heard you cleared the Tide road. First pint's on me when you're back.
UI.BrassSailor3: My brother came up out of the fog yesterday, on the harbour road. Two years! He asked what's for supper.
UI.BrassGossip1: That bell tower's been silent forty years. Old Hobb still climbs it every morning.
UI.BrassGossip2: The Council says the Kindling will make solid ground of all the Murk. Imagine. Walking anywhere!
UI.BrassGossip3: The bells woke the whole town. Then the whole Murk. Then my husband, finally.
UI.BrassKid1: If you shout into the fog, sometimes it hums back. Mum says I'm making it up.
UI.BrassKid2: I SHOUTED at the fog and it HUMMED back! Everyone believes me now!
UI.BrassDock1: Harbour post's capped by Council order. Nobody walks the Tide road.
UI.BrassDock2: You're walking the Tide road with Miss Vane? Rather you than me.
UI.Hobb1: EH? Speak up! The bells took the top end of my ears forty years back!
UI.Hobb2: WE'RE GOING TO THE TIDE LANTERWAY!
UI.Hobb3: The tide's a lantern? No it isn't. Sit down, you look peaky.
UI.Hobb4: Hobb. Tell them what you told me. About the bells.
UI.Hobb5: Ah! The bells. Before lamps, ringers walked the roads. You rang, and the Murk let you pass. You asked it nicely.
UI.Hobb6: Then the Council said lamps were modern and bells were superstition. Tied the clappers, they did. Forty years quiet.
UI.Hobb7: Does he mean the fog... listens?
UI.Hobb10: Course it does. Everything listens. Except me. Here, take this. Ring it when the dark gets close. Won't save you. Might help.
UI.Hobb11: The harbour post is capped, but I know the Council's lock. Let's go to the harbour.
UI.HobbIdle: WHAT? Oh, it's you. The bells are still tied, if you're asking.
UI.Maw1: The fog heaves. A vast mouth opens out of the Murk!
UI.Maw2: That is not a fish. That is a building with teeth.
UI.Maw3: Pell... look. Down there, under the surface.
UI.Maw4: Deep in the grey, a sleeping face drifts past, and is gone.
UI.Maw5: That was a person. Asleep. Pell, the people in the Murk are... sleeping?
UI.Maw6: Maybe it was only the fog playing tricks.
UI.Maw7: Maybe. ...Maybe Tobin is down there, dreaming.
UI.Maw8: Then we'll find a way to wake him. I promise.
UI.Maw10: I just did. Wickwardens are stubborn. It's all the walking.
UI.Maw11: Ahem. Glimmerhold's that way. I'll just... be over there. Being a cook.
UI.SignGlimmerhold: GLIMMERHOLD, seat of the Lamp Council. Hall: north. Vault: south. Spire Road: east.
UI.SignFounder: 'Light is order.' Founder of the Lamp Council. Someone has chalked underneath: 'order is boring'.
UI.GuardVault: The Lamp Vault is sealed by order of the High Lampwarden.
UI.GuardEast: The Spire Road is closed until the Kindling. Move along.
UI.CinderLighter1: Five days to the Kindling! After that, they say we'll never need to walk another road.
UI.CinderLighter2: The High Lampwarden sent you down the Spire road? Nobody comes back from that.
UI.CinderLighter3: No more lamps to light. I'm learning the handbell. It's harder than it looks.
UI.CinderCitizen1: Solid fog, forever. Think of the property prices.
UI.CinderCitizen2: The guards say traitors were marched off the Spire road. They looked like children to me.
UI.CinderKid1: Can I come to the Kindling? Mum says it's past my bedtime. It's at noon.
UI.CinderKid2: The big lamp went out and the sky got nicer.
UI.Councillor1: The High Lampwarden is not to be disturbed. He is... composing himself.
UI.Councillor2: Between us, the Lampwarden hasn't slept properly in ten years. Not since his daughter.
UI.HallClerk1: Ah, the 'traitors'. Paperwork says you're dead. Shall I amend it?
UI.HallClerk2: Form 1, Abolition of the Kindling, filed and approved. In triplicate.
UI.AshgraveWait: The Vault lies beneath the city. Bring me the Heartwick, wickwarden.
UI.Speech1: Wickwardens! For three hundred years we have walked thin roads over a hungry sea.
UI.Speech2: In five days, the Everlamp atop the Wick Spire will be kindled. Its light will reach every corner of the Murk.
UI.Speech3: And the Murk will harden. Forever. One solid land. No more roads. No more sinking.
UI.Speech5: High Lampwarden! The outer holds have no oil. People are sinking on dark roads right now.
UI.Speech6: Sacrifices, young man. After the Kindling there will be no dark roads left to sink on. Patience.
UI.Speech7: You are the ones who cleared the Tide Lanterway? Then I have work for you.
UI.Speech8: Beneath this city lies the old Lamp Vault. In it rests the Heartwick: the first flame, the only wick that can light the Everlamp.
UI.Speech9: Captain Marrow will guide you. Captain?
UI.Speech13: She carries a lantern that's also a mace. Or a mace that's also a lantern. Either way, I'm in love.
UI.Speech14: Captain Ines Marrow, Lamp Guard. I'll take you down to the Vault. Keep up, and don't touch anything that glows.
UI.Journal1: A brass plaque: 'The Murk is not vapour. It is many, each smaller than dust, crowded close.' - The first wickwardens.
UI.Journal2: A brass plaque: 'Light stills them. Stilled, they bear our weight. Stilled too long, they do not wake.'
UI.Journal3: A brass plaque: 'Light a road, yes. Light the sea, never. Where you can, ring for passage instead.'
UI.Journal4: A brass plaque, half melted. Only one line remains: '...they keep the fallen warm...'
UI.SignPedestal: The empty pedestal of the Heartwick.
UI.Warden1: Brass grinds on brass. The Vault's old guardian wakes and turns its lamp-eye on the party!
UI.Warden2: Positions! It's built to stop thieves. Let's show it we're not thieves. We're worse.
UI.Warden3: On the pedestal, a short black wick glows like a coal that will never cool: the Heartwick.
UI.Warden4: Pell. The plaques. If the Everlamp lights the whole Murk...
UI.Warden5: It stills all of it. Forever. It kills it.
UI.Warden8: The High Lampwarden can't know this. We'll tell him. He'll stop.
UI.Betray1: The Heartwick. Splendid. Hand it over, wickwarden.
UI.Betray2: High Lampwarden, the plaques in the Vault... the Murk is alive. The Kindling would kill it, and everyone sunk inside it.
UI.Betray3: Sunk people are dead people, boy. I have known that for a very long time.
UI.Betray4: Fog is fog. I will hold it still if it takes every lamp in the world. Captain, take the wick from him.
UI.Betray7: I swore an oath to keep the roads, not to you. I won't help you drown a sea.
UI.Betray8: Then walk the roads you love so much. Guards! The Spire road. Snuff the posts behind them.
UI.Betray9: They are marched onto the Spire road at spearpoint. Post by post, the lamps go out behind them.
UI.Betray10: The fog softens underfoot like wet snow. Then there is nothing beneath them at all.
UI.Betray11: Pell! Grab my apron! Grab my...
UI.Wake1: ...Grey. Soft. Quiet. And, against all sense, breath.
UI.Wake4: Odge, here. Lost a shoe. Kept the pan.
UI.Wake6: All around them, in hollows of fog, hundreds of people sleep, wrapped in grey like moths in silk.
UI.UnderNotYet: Someone has been watching us since we landed. We should find them first.
UI.DriftNotYet: Not yet. First, the moth village. Light that does not hurt.
UI.UnderSleeper2: Huh? Bells? Is it morning? Which morning?
UI.Hush1: Many... saw you fall. Many... caught you.
UI.Hush2: That face. That's Tobin's face! How do you have my brother's face?!
UI.Hush3: Borrowed. From one asleep in the grove. Sorry. Will change.
UI.Hush4: The figure blurs into a pale, gentle shape with no face at all.
UI.Hush5: Better? We are Hush. One of many. Sent to speak, because many cannot.
UI.Hush6: You're the Murk. The whole fog... is you.
UI.Hush7: Yes. Your lights are cold. When light stays, we sleep. When it stays very long, we stop.
UI.Hush8: The sleepers are your fallen ones. We hold them. Keep them warm. Wait for the ringing. Nobody rings any more.
UI.Hush10: The Big Light comes soon. It will stop us. All of us. And them.
UI.Hush11: Then help us get back up. We'll stop it.
UI.Hush12: Yes. Hush walks with you. Hush has never walked before. Is it hard?
UI.Hush14: First, the moth village. East. Light that is asked for, not forced.
UI.Nim1: STRANGERS! Up-people! Real up-people! Do you have the sky? Is it big? Is it really blue?
UI.Nim3: I'm Nim! I sank when I was a baby and the moths raised me. Well, Elder Wenna raised me. The moths helped.
UI.Nim4: Some of the sunk wake on their own, travellers. Not many. We made a home where the moths glow.
UI.Nim5: Moth light is asked for, not forced. The Murk does not mind it.
UI.Nim6: Moth light is warm. We like it.
UI.Nim7: You're going UP? Take me! I want the sky! I've got my net and my moths, and I bite.
UI.Nim9: I'll be good! Mostly! I'll only bite bad things!
UI.Nim10: Rest by my fire before you go. Hush says your Tobin sleeps at the east end of the grove, surveyor.
UI.Wenna1: Welcome, falling ones. You are not the first to land soft.
UI.Mothfolk1: I sank on a fishing road twenty years ago. Woke up last spring. My wife has remarried. Twice.
UI.Mothfolk2: The bells! I heard the bells! I'm going home. Well, to visit.
UI.Mothfolk3: Do not shout at the moths. They are shy, and they remember.
UI.Mothfolk4: The fog hums differently since the ringing. Happier, I think.
UI.Cocoon0: A sleeper wrapped in grey silk. It breathes slow and even.
UI.Cocoon1: A young man sleeps in the grey silk, a pencil still tucked behind his ear.
UI.Cocoon2: Tobin... He's warm. He's breathing. He's smiling, the idiot.
UI.Cocoon3: The bells could wake him. We'll ring them, Ottilie. I swear it on every lamp in Tallowby.
UI.Cocoon4: Then hurry, wickwarden. I have two years of shouting saved up for him.
UI.Campfire1: Sit, sit. The moths will keep watch tonight.
UI.Campfire2: Later, by the moth fire. The others are asleep. Mostly.
UI.Campfire5: When this is over... would you walk a road with me? A new one. One nobody has charted yet.
UI.Campfire8: I wanted to be sure you heard.
UI.Campfire12: Quiet, all of you. Some of us are pretending not to listen.
UI.Stilled1: That one stayed in the light too long. It hurts. It does not know you. Please... let it rest.
UI.Stilled3: It sleeps now. Truly. Thank you.
UI.Stilled4: The fog gathers beneath the party, firm as a held breath, and begins to rise.
UI.Rise1: The party steps off the fog onto the road outside Tallowby. It is night, and the village is full of masked figures.
UI.Rise2: Is THIS the sky? It's black! You said it was blue!
UI.Night1: Pell?! You're alive! They said you'd been... oh, Pell.
UI.Night2: Hesk's been out every night. With them. He's at the Lamp House now.
UI.Night3: I know, Marta. I'm going to talk to him.
UI.Reveal1: ...Pell. The Murk gave you back. I hoped it would.
UI.Reveal2: You're the Old Man. You're the leader of the Snuffers.
UI.Reveal3: I've been cutting wicks for six years. Slowing the oil to Glimmerhold. Buying the Murk some time.
UI.Reveal4: People sank on those roads! Because you cut them!
UI.Reveal5: ...Fewer than you'd think. I rang for every one I could. But not all of them. I carry those.
UI.Reveal6: Your trial on the Spur. I had those wicks cut. I wanted you to see a dark road with your own eyes.
UI.Reveal7: You lied to me my whole life.
UI.Reveal8: I did. Now let's see if I taught you anything true. Show me you can walk your own road, Pell.
UI.Reveal9: Ha... You hit things with the pole. Just like I said.
UI.Reveal10: The bells of Brassmouth hang tied. Hobb knows the tune, but not the words. Here is the old score; the Council burned the rest.
UI.Reveal11: Ring the Passage Song, and the Murk will lift every sleeper onto the roads. Gently. Then go and stop Ashgrave.
UI.Reveal12: And take a ringer's trick: ring at the old bell posts on the roads, and the fog will carry you between the holds.
UI.Reveal13: And when it's done, both of you are coming home for supper. Hesk, you're doing the dishes. For six years.
UI.HeskTalk17: Go on. Hobb's waiting in his tower. He's been waiting forty years.
UI.HeskTalk19: The whole Murk hums like a kettle. I never thought I'd hear it again.
UI.TowerBlocked: Fallen beams and old rope block the stairs. Hobb would know a way up.
UI.HobbJoin1: You found the score?! Hesk, the old rascal. He owes me nine pints and a bell rope.
UI.HobbJoin2: Hobb, will you ring it with us?
UI.HobbJoin3: WHAT? ...I'm joking. I heard that one. I've been waiting forty years to hear that one.
UI.HobbJoin4: The clappers are tied at the top, and something's nested in the great bell. Something that eats copper.
UI.HobbJoin5: I'll catch it in my net!
UI.HobbJoin6: That's the spirit, small one. Up we go! Mind the eleventh step. It bites too.
UI.Verdi1: A long green shape uncoils from the great bell, dripping verdigris.
UI.Verdi2: So YOU'RE what's been eating my bell! Forty years of copper! Get it!
UI.Ring1: Now then. The Passage Song. Pell, you pull. I'll count. ONE...
UI.Ring2: For the first time in forty years, the great bells of Brassmouth ring.
UI.Ring3: Across the Murk the fog stirs, swells, and rises gently, carrying the sleepers up onto the roads.
UI.Tobin1: ...Tilly? Why is everyone crying? Did I miss lunch?
UI.Tobin2: Two years, you idiot! You missed two years of lunches!
UI.Tobin3: And who's the wickwarden standing so close to you?
UI.Tobin6: Far to the east a white glare climbs the sky. The Wick Spire is burning early.
UI.Tobin7: Ashgrave heard the bells. He's lighting the Everlamp now.
UI.Tobin8: Many... feel it. It is cold. Hurry.
UI.Tobin9: To Glimmerhold, then. The Spire road is open.
UI.TobinTalk: Tilly says you hold charts upside down. I like you already.
UI.Brask2: Sergeant Brask. You taught me to march. Don't make me teach you how to fall.
UI.Brask3: HA! Big words for a... is that a cook?
UI.Brask5: ...Go on, Captain. I never did like heights.
UI.Brask6: Get your men off the Spire, Brask. Go home.
UI.Final1: You rang the bells. Do you know what you've done? You've filled my roads with ghosts.
UI.Final2: They're not ghosts! They're people! My brother walked out of the Murk this morning!
UI.Final3: ...Then where is my Liss? She sank ten years ago on the Spire road. I didn't ring. I lit lamps. I lit every lamp I could.
UI.Final4: If the sunk can come back, then I left her down there. For ten years. No. NO. It's fog. It's only fog.
UI.Final5: The Everlamp will hold it still, and I will walk out across it and find her.
UI.Final6: You'll kill her, if she's down there. You'll kill all of them.
UI.Final8: The Everlamp roars. Its light pours down the Spire, hard and white.
UI.Final9: It is burning by itself! It will not stop!
UI.Final10b: Many... lend you their warmth. Stand. Once more.
UI.Final11: The great lamp gutters, flickers, and goes dark. Far below, the Murk sighs.
UI.Final12: ...Papa? It's so bright up here. Why are you crying?
UI.Final13: Liss... Liss. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. I should have rung for you.
UI.Final14: I heard bells. I followed them. It was a long way.
UI.Final15: She was held. She was warm. Always.
UI.Final16: Let's go home. All of us.
UI.Epi2: Form 1, Abolition of Form 12-B: approved. At last. I may cry.
UI.Epi4: I SAID YOU'RE OFF THE BEAT, YOU OLD BELL.
UI.Epi5: Apple and candlenut pie. I made it for you. For the ninth time.
UI.Epi8: Hush, look! The sky! It's... grey again.
UI.Epi9: Grey is a good colour. It suits it.
UI.Epi10: The lamps are going out one by one. On purpose, this time.
UI.Epi11: And the bell posts are going up. Hobb's teaching half of Tallowby to ring.
UI.Epi12: Here. A chart. Blank. For the road we haven't walked yet.
UI.Epi14: Obviously. You'd only hold it upside down.
UI.End1: The lamps of the Murk went dark, one by one, and nobody sank.
UI.End2: Where the lamps had been, bells were hung, and travellers rang for passage.
UI.End3: Hesk and Hobb argued about the tempo of every single one.
UI.End4: Ashgrave gave up the Council's chain. He rings the Spire road bell every dawn, with Liss beside him.
UI.End5: Gorse and the farmers of Farrow's Reach walk home on humming roads.
UI.End6: Bram opened a kitchen at the Brassmouth harbour. The captain eats there every day. For inspection purposes.
UI.End7: Nim saw a blue sky at last, on her father's shoulders. She did not bite it.
UI.End8: Hush learned to walk, to laugh, and to borrow faces only when asked.
UI.End9: Tobin and Ottilie charted the breathing of the Murk together, and argued about the ink.
UI.End10: And Pell and Ottilie set out on a road nobody had walked yet.
UI.End12: THE END. Thank you for walking with us.
UI.EndSaveAsk: Write the finished journey in a slot?
UI.TrialNeed: %1 should be in the party for this.
UI.ArenaHello: The Trial Hall. Three fights, one rule. Your pick.
UI.ArenaLost: The keeper helps you up. Come back any time.
UI.Hush10b: Some of us are hurt. Too long in light, they forget. They will bite you. Do not be sorry.
UI.Hush10c: Fallen lamps sink too. Down here they still burn, and they are angry.
UI.Gorse8b: The Old Man's crew has cut wicks for years. Us farmers only joined them this spring.
UI.Reveal5b: My Snuffers hum the old passage notes. The fog lets them cross. That was my 'trick'.
UI.Reveal10b: A song needs an answer from below. For six years nobody down there answered me. You walk with one who can.
UI.Reveal10c: I sank once, as a boy. One of Hobb's bells brought me up. I never forgot.
UI.TalOld4: Pell! We'd buried you, lad. Well, in talk.
UI.TalKid4: The Snuffers slept in our barn. They snore like lamps.
UI.TalMiller4: Hesk is finally doing the dishes. Marta is counting the plates.
UI.CinderLighter4: The Spire is burning early! The sky's gone white. It wasn't meant to do that.
UI.CinderKid3: The big lamp stings my eyes. Mum says don't look. I'm looking.
UI.HallClerk3: The Lampwarden went up alone. He signed no form at all. Most alarming.
UI.HonQuest1: I brought you a jar of candlenut honey, ma'am. From the press.
UI.HonQuest2: Finally, someone who listens! Pell, take your old wake-up bell. For the boy who sleeps on roofs.
UI.Roof1: That night Pell wakes on the roof, one hand reaching for the weathervane.
UI.Roof2: All this time I wanted to light the dark. Maybe I only had to talk to it.
UI.Roof3: He climbs down quietly. His boots, for once, stay downstairs.
UI.Chart1: Wait. The current turns here. What the tide swallows, it always gives back a little further on.
UI.Chart2: There, in the firm fog: a coin, shining. The chart was right.
UI.Form1: A Form 12-B? Filled in? I... I need to sit down.
UI.Form2: Declared dead, so paid as dead. Here is your back pay. In triplicate.
UI.SignLiss: A portrait: a little girl holding a lantern. A brass plate: LISS.
UI.SignSunkLedger: The ledger of the sunk. Ten years back, one line: 'Liss, Spire road'. Crossed out, then written again.
UI.SignTobinNotes: Tobin's notebook: 'The fog breathes. If it breathes, it listens.'
UI.HushGift: Many... wove this for you, Pell. For walking. Not for fighting. A little for fighting.
UI.HobbJoin7: Here, my spare ear trumpet. Hold it to your ear when the bells go. Or don't, see if I care.
UI.SignFarrow: FARROW'S REACH. Its roads have started humming.
UI.Farrow1: The farmers are learning to ring. It's out of tune, but the fog is patient.
UI.Farrow2: Six weeks in the dark. We'll never trust a lamp again.
UI.GorseShared1: The wickwarden who left us half! That oil held our roads until the bells came.
UI.GorseShared2: Take this. An old-timers' match. It catches even in fog.
UI.GorseKept1: You. You took it all back, that night. We lost two of ours on the road.
UI.GorseKept2: ...But you rang the bells. They came back up. We're square, wickwarden.
UI.TPell1: The old ringers' road. It sinks into the fog like a stair.
UI.TPell2: A figure holds a pole lit at both ends. It doesn't see you: it waits for a lamp.
UI.TPell3: She kept herself lit for three hundred years. She can rest now.
UI.TBram1: A sunken kitchen. The stove is cold. Granny Odge sank right here when I was small.
UI.TBram2: The kettle is whistling by itself. Something is guarding this kitchen. Badly.
UI.TBram3: Her pan. The heaviest ever forged. I'll take it home. Her too, once the bells wake her.
UI.TOtt1: The road where Tobin sank. He was surveying it. His stakes are still in the fog.
UI.TOtt2: Something is eating the currents. That's why my charts never matched.
UI.TOtt3: His meridian needles. Tobin, you idiot, you left these here for me on purpose.
UI.TInes1: Under the vault, the old hall of the captains. Every one swore to keep the roads.
UI.TInes2: The first captain still guards the door. She asks for the oath.
UI.TInes3: She handed me the Beacon. I'll keep the roads. Even the ones without lamps.
UI.THush1: The stillwater. Here many stopped for good.
UI.THush2: A hollow sleeper. It forgot it was dreaming. Help it remember.
UI.THush3: It remembers. It beats, slowly. It gave us its heart.
UI.TNim1: The canopy! Wenna says no child climbs up here. I'm not a child, I bite.
UI.TNim2: The old moth. She has watched every sunk one fall. She tests those who want to go back up.
UI.TNim3: The thousandwing net. Every moth in the grove helped weave it. For you, Nim.
UI.THobb1: The belltower cellar. They threw the Passage bell down here when the Council banned bells.
UI.THobb2: It rang alone, in the dark, for forty years. It got... odd.
UI.THobb3: Ha! I heard that one. Every bit of it. It was never out of tune, it was me who was deaf.
UI.Root1: The candlenut roots shift. Something very old wakes under the orchard.
UI.Root2: She sleeps again. The orchard will bear double this year.
UI.Levi1: The Drift opens. A back longer than a road rises out of the fog.
UI.Levi2: It dives again, without anger. Hush says it only wanted to play.
UI.BraskNim1: That little one... She has her mother's chin. And that yell. I know that yell.
UI.BraskNim2: My girl sank on the Farm road eleven years ago. She was one. She already bit.
UI.BraskNim3: ...You smell of soup and gunpowder. Wenna said my papa smelled like that.
UI.BraskNim4: After. After the lamp, we'll talk. Go on, little one. Go bite the right thing.
UI.LearnPeal: Pell rings Hobb's old handbell against his pole. The fog answers.
UI.InesSleeper1: A guard sleeps in the grey silk, the Guard's badge still pinned on.
UI.InesSleeper2: That's Dorran. My first winter on patrol. I signed the report: 'lost on the road'.
UI.InesSleeper3: He wasn't lost. He was waiting. I'll come back for you, soldier.
UI.InesSleeper4: He sleeps. He is warm. Many keep him for you.
UI.HobbGuest1: I'll walk you to the harbour post. The fog knows my bells. AND MY KNEES.
UI.HobbGuest2: Right. My knees say: the tower. Off you go, young ones. Ring loud, ring true!
UI.HobbLeft: Hobb heads back to his tower.
UI.Report8: One more thing. You fought out on the Spur, didn't you? I can see it on you. Every true blow stokes the flame in a wickwarden.
UI.Report9: Let it build. When it burns full, let it all go at once. We call that a Bright. Save it for when it matters.
UI.DuoReady_lampandbell: WHAT? Your flame and my bell, together! Keep the glow half full and I'll ring along with you.
UI.DuoReady_northlight: I've charted how you move, Pell. With half the glow, we could light the way together.
UI.DuoReady_greywings: Hush and me can do a moth thing now! It needs half the glow. Please?
UI.DuoReady_messhall: Captain, I have a recipe for two. Half the glow, and the whole party eats.
UI.DuoReady_deepchart: Many... see the currents with you. Half the glow, and we chart them deep.
UI.SealedSunken: The old road just stops here and drops into bare fog. No post, no lamp. Nobody walks that without a light.
UI.SealedSurvey: Old survey stakes run on into the bare fog, then nothing. It won't hold me past the last one.
UI.SealedFarrow: The road to Farrow's Reach, every post on it cut. Gorse's people walk it in the dark somehow. I can't. Not yet.
UI.SpurLook: Hm? There's a light on the Spur... and someone standing by it.
UI.SpurSnuffed: The figure leans over the post. The flame dies, and the fog closes in.
UI.HobbWatch: Hobb, the Watchlight of the coast stands east of the harbour. Will you light it with us?
UI.TideWatchNext: The Watchlight of the Tideway is just past here. Light it, and the wall before Glimmerhold falls.
UI.IsletRevealed: The Veil lifts from the whole islet!
UI.PageFound: Found a page for the Round Book: %1
UI.EchoHeard: The fog thickens, and a memory rises out of it...
UI.WatchLights: The great brazier catches. Its fire climbs high over the Murk, and far off the Murk Wall sinks back into the fog.
UI.WatchLit: The brazier of the Watchlight burns high over the fog.
UI.WatchLights_rive: The way east is open. Wickhollow is past the wall.
UI.WatchLights_east: The wall to the south is gone. On to Brassmouth.
UI.WatchLights_coast: The Tideway is open. Hold on to your hats.
UI.WatchLights_tide: There it is: Glimmerhold, shining over the water.
UI.WatchLights_spire: The road to the Spire is clear. This ends tonight.
UI.WatchLocked_rive: The great lantern is dry. Master Hesk will know what to do with it.
UI.WatchLocked_east: A brass plate: LIGHTING BY AUTHORISED PERSONS ONLY (FORM 12-B).
UI.WatchLocked_coast: The lantern's gears are stuck with forty years of salt. A ringer would know how they turn.
UI.WatchLocked_tide: Something in the water below makes the whole tower shake. Not now.
UI.WatchLocked_spire: The lantern room is barred from the inside. Someone does not want this lit. Not yet.
UI.BookHelp_pages: Pages torn from the Round Book of the Shore Watchlight.
UI.BookHelp_echoes: Memories the fog kept. A to hear one again.
UI.BookHelp_quests: The lost folk of the Murk Sea.
UI.BookHelp_map: The islets the Veil gave back.
UI.Echo_firstflame_1: A woman in a patched coat kneels on the bare fog with a jar of glimmer oil.
UI.Echo_firstflame_2: "Hold still," she whispers to the fog, "I only want to see." A wick catches.
UI.Echo_firstflame_3: The fog under her knees hardens to stone. Behind her, a whole village holds its breath.
UI.Echo_drownedvillage_1: Night on the Tideway. A row of lamps, then one gutters, then the next.
UI.Echo_drownedvillage_2: Houses slide into the fog as gently as boats leaving a dock. Nobody screams. Somebody rings a bell, once.
UI.Echo_drownedvillage_3: Then only water-sounds, and very far below, the humming takes the bell's note and keeps it.
UI.Echo_lissleaves_1: A girl with a pocket lantern stands at the last post of the Spire road.
UI.Echo_lissleaves_2: She tucks the lantern into her coat, so the singing won't be shy, and steps off the stones.
UI.Echo_lissleaves_3: The fog lifts her like a hand lifts a bird. She doesn't look back. She is smiling.
UI.Echo_twofriends_1: Two young wickwardens sit on a causeway, poles across their knees, sharing a bun.
UI.Echo_twofriends_2: "Ash, listen. It hums." "Hesk, you're mad. Lights are for keeping things out."
UI.Echo_twofriends_3: They laugh, and the one called Ash glances at the fog a little too long.
UI.Echo_firstsnuff_1: A farmer with hollow cheeks reaches up to a burning lamp with shears.
UI.Echo_firstsnuff_2: "My children need the oil more than the road does." Snip. The flame drowns.
UI.Echo_firstsnuff_3: An old man in a long coat steps out of the dark and says: "Not like that. Like this. Quietly."
UI.Echo_onebell_1: A storm night at the coast. A young ringer hauls on the great bell, again, again.
UI.Echo_onebell_2: "Ring them home, Hobb! Ring!" The bronze roars until the air itself is ringing.
UI.Echo_onebell_3: When the boats are in, he cannot hear the cheering. He laughs anyway, because he can see it.
UI.Echo_braskleaves_1: A big soldier walks the Farm road at night, ringing a cowbell, calling a small name.
UI.Echo_braskleaves_2: Dawn comes. He sits on the last post and holds the bell until it is cold.
UI.Echo_braskleaves_3: Then he leaves it on the stones and walks to Glimmerhold without turning around.
UI.Echo_thevote_1: A long table in Glimmerhold. Twelve councillors. One empty chair, for a sunk colleague.
UI.Echo_thevote_2: "All in favour of the Everlamp." Hands rise. Ashgrave's is first, and shaking.
UI.Echo_thevote_3: "Then the fog will hold still," he says, "and I will walk out and find her."
UI.Echo_softvoice_1: A small boy is lost in the Veil, crying. The fog around him starts, very softly, to hum.
UI.Echo_softvoice_2: A pale shape kneels beside him. "Don't be... sad. Many are here. Keeping you warm."
UI.Echo_softvoice_3: It points the way to a lamp. It doesn't follow. It has no face yet, only kindness.
UI.Echo_lastferry_1: An old ferryman poles a flat boat across the fog between two islets, lantern at the bow.
UI.Echo_lastferry_2: "Last crossing," he tells his passengers. "The Council's building stone roads. Faster, they say."
UI.Echo_lastferry_3: He ties the boat up at the harbour and leaves the lantern burning in it, just in case.
UI.QuestNote_ferry_started: Light the lamp of the wreck islet for him.
UI.QuestNote_ferry_done: The ferry runs to the far shoal again.
UI.QuestNote_wisp_started: The child ran home. See the miller.
UI.QuestNote_wisp_done: The miller's child is safe at home.
UI.QuestNote_courier_started: Find the pages on the Reach and the Nutshell.
UI.QuestNote_courier_done: The courier gave you his page.
UI.QuestNote_deserter_done: You helped a Snuffer choose his way.

UI.QuestNote_carto_done: The chart now shows every islet.

UI.QuestNote_main_3: Light the last post on the Spur, then go back to Hesk.

UI.QuestNote_main_6: See Clerk Pottle at the lamp office in Wickhollow.

UI.Ferry1: Is someone there? I can't see a thing. Forty years I poled this fog and I never once got lost on it.
UI.Ferry2: There's a lamp on this islet, dead as a doornail. If someone lit it, I'd find my way back to my old dock.
UI.Ferry3: Light! Bless your wick. Now I see where I am: the wreck of my own boat, would you believe.
UI.Ferry4: Come to the harbour dock, wickwarden. I've one more crossing in these arms, to the far shoal nobody visits.
UI.Wisp1: The little lights went this way... and that way... and now I don't know any way.
UI.Wisp2: Tallowby is back west. Follow the lamps, the ones that burn, and you'll be home before supper.
UI.Wisp3: Lamps are boring. But okay. Don't tell my mum about the wisps!
UI.WispThanks1: My boy came home muddy to the ears, talking about a wickwarden who showed him the way.
UI.WispThanks2: He found this in the fog and kept it for you. He says it's a song. It's very crumpled.
UI.Courier1: Clerk Pottle sent me to gather loose pages from the fog, for the archive. I found one, but he wants a set, and now I'm lost.
UI.Courier2: They say two more lie on the Reach, up north, and on that little Nutshell islet. Find them, and I'll trade you mine.
UI.Courier3: You found them both! The Clerk's archive can wait. This one's yours.
UI.Deserter1: Don't shout. I'm not cutting anything. I'm done cutting.
UI.Deserter2: You're one of the Old Man's crew.
UI.Deserter3: Was. I'm a farmer. I want to go home, but they'll call me a coward at Farrow. Or I could just walk into the fog.
UI.Deserter4: Home. Yes. A coward who comes home is still home. Thank you.
UI.Deserter5: Then I'll walk. Maybe the fog's kinder than people say.
UI.FarrowDeserterHome: My nephew came back from the roads. Thin as a rake. He says a wickwarden sent him home. Bless you.
UI.FarrowDeserterGone: One of ours walked off into the fog, they say. Some nights I hear him humming out there. Happy, I think.
UI.Carto1: A chart of the Murk Sea! Nobody has drawn one since the Watchlights went dark.
UI.Carto2: I need to see the Tideway. Light its first three lamps and I'll fill in every islet I can glimpse.
UI.Carto3: There! And there! I can see clear to the Capital. My hand can't keep up.
UI.Carto4: Here, copy it into your book. Every islet, even the ones the Veil still hides.
UI.CartoMap: The chart of the Round Book now shows every islet of the Murk Sea.
UI.Carto5: Mind the islets marked with a little x. I have no idea what those are. Neither do you, I bet.
UI.Merchant1: My barge ran aground in this Veil, and my oil with it. I sell lamp oil! In the dark! The irony!
UI.Merchant2: If the lamps on the rocks and at the East landing burned, I could lead my mule the whole way.
UI.Merchant3: Light, all the way to the landing! I'll set up there. Come and see me, wickwarden. Friends' prices.
UI.MerchantHello: Oil, buns, little lanterns! Friends' prices for the one who lit my way.
UI.Home_talodd1: I kept a tower once, the one on the shore. Now I keep a kettle. It whistles less than the fog did.
UI.Home_talodd2: That's my tower's book! Torn to ribbons... no. Torn with care, one page at a time. Whoever did it wanted those pages found.
UI.Home_talodd3: So now you know about Hesk. I knew the first night he came home with soot on his gloves. I said nothing. Keepers keep things.
UI.Home_talodd4: Hear that? Bells on the shore road. I waited my whole life to hear the fog answer. Open the window, would you? Let it in.
UI.Look_talodd_spyglass: A brass spyglass on a stand by the window, turned toward the shore. The lens is polished. Its owner is not done watching.
UI.Home_talmill1: Mum says I can't go past the last lamp any more. So I draw the wisps instead. They hold still on paper.
UI.Home_talmill2: The bells ring on the roads now, and the wisps dance to them. I KNEW they liked music.
UI.Look_talmill_drawings: Drawings of little lights pinned all over the wall. In one of them, a wickwarden with a very long pole.
UI.Home_talfenn1: Your trial today? I took mine from Hesk's old master. Lit three posts and fell in a ditch. Passed anyway.
UI.Home_talfenn2: See that bell? I was a ringer, forty years back, before the Council tied them all. I still polish it on Sundays.
UI.Home_talfenn3: I heard the bells from my bed. Forty years! I got up and rang mine at the window like a fool. A happy fool.
UI.Look_talfenn_bell: A small handbell, polished bright. Its clapper is tied with a faded ribbon stamped with the Council seal.
UI.Look_talempty_table: A table laid for four under a grey coat of dust. The bread was never cut.
UI.Look_talempty_letter: A letter on the shelf: 'Gone to my sister's past the Spur. The oil's not coming and the nights are long. Water the beans if you pass.'
UI.Knock_tallowby: Nobody answers. It smells of warm bread.
UI.Home_wickbunk1: Twelve hours at the press, then twelve hours of snoring in here. Mind the boots. Mind ALL the boots.
UI.Home_wickbunk2: The Council raised the quota again. Look at the board. We press, Glimmerhold drinks it, and the small holds go dark.
UI.Home_wickbunk3: The quota board is coming down. We press what the holds need, and the rest of the day we nap. On purpose.
UI.Look_wickbunk_board: A chalk board: GLIMMER QUOTA, 40 BARRELS A WEEK. Underneath, someone has drawn a very tired face.
UI.Home_wickprune1: Grafting knives, all of them. A candlenut tree takes a cutting the way a child takes advice: slowly, and only from the right person.
UI.Home_wickprune2: You look hungry. Everyone your age looks hungry. Here.
UI.Home_wickprune3: Every tree in the orchard came from one I grafted. Well, most. The crooked ones are my sister's.
UI.Home_wickprune4: The trees hum when the bells ring. Sixty years of grafting and I never heard that. Never too old to be surprised.
UI.Look_wickprune_knives: Grafting knives hung by size, each with its own name burnt into the handle.
UI.Look_wickodge_recipes: A book of recipes in a round, kind hand. 'Stew for a sad day.' 'Stew for a very sad day.'
UI.Home_wickodge_bram: Gran's book. One recipe for every kind of day. I learned to read on that one. 'Add more onion.'
UI.Look_wickodge_buffet: In the buffet, a crock of stew and a note: 'For Bram, or whoever he brings. The neighbours.'
UI.Look_wickodge_empty: The buffet is empty but for a clean cloth.
UI.Knock_wickhollow: A sign on the door: CLOSED FOR THE HARVEST.
UI.Home_wickguard1: I keep watch at night. Saw a Snuffer once. Well, a shadow. A big shadow. I drew it, look.
UI.Home_wickguard2: The Snuffers are only farmers, they say? Then my poster is wrong. I'm keeping it. It's my best drawing.
UI.Home_wickguard3: Nothing to watch now but the fog, and it just hums. I've taken up knitting. Night knitting.
UI.Look_wickguard_poster: WANTED: SNUFFERS. The drawing shows a tall thing with six arms and a very small hat.
UI.Home_wickcarter1: The cart for Tallowby? Loaded three days ago. Then the Snuffers took the barrels before I'd found my hat.
UI.Home_wickcarter2: I drive every barrel to Glimmerhold now. Every last one. The small holds get a line in my ledger and nothing else.
UI.Home_wickcarter3: Back on the old round: Tallowby, Brassmouth, Farrow's Reach. The roads hum under the wheels. The horse loves it.
UI.Look_wickcarter_ledger: The carter's ledger: 'Tallowby, 4 barrels, LATE.' LATE is underlined three times, crossed out, then written again.
UI.Home_brasssail1: Sails for ships that can't leave the dock. I keep sewing. When the Tide road opens they'll all want one at once.
UI.Home_brasssail2: The Tide road's open! Six sails sold this week. Six. I had to sit down.
UI.Home_brasssail3: I sewed the sail of the last ferry, before the fog took the crossings. They say the ferryman's home. I'd like to see that sail again.
UI.Look_brasssail_sail: A half-sewn sail on its frame. Stitched very small in one corner: 'for whoever sails next'.
UI.Home_brassbell1: My husband cast bells. Then the Council tied them all and nobody ordered another. He kept casting anyway. Out of spite, he said.
UI.Home_brassbell2: Do you hear them? That's his bell, the middle one. He cast it the year we married. Took me forty years to hear it ring.
UI.Look_brassbell_mould: A bell mould, cracked down the middle. Scratched inside: 'The last one. They'll ring again.'
UI.Home_brassfish1: Fancy a hand of Gull's Eye? Twenty glimmer to sit down.
UI.Home_brassfish2: ...Well, I'll be. Beaten by a wickwarden. Take the pot.
UI.Home_brassfish4: Suit yourself. The gulls will play me.
UI.Home_brassfish5: No more cards for you. You've got the luck of a gull in a fish barrel.
UI.Look_brassfish_cards: A sticky deck of cards. The gull's eye card has been nibbled. Probably by a gull.
UI.Home_brassport1: Tide road dark, harbour post capped by Council order. I sign the tide tables and nobody sails. Best paid nap in Brassmouth.
UI.Home_brassport2: Ships out again! I had forgotten how loud a harbour is.
UI.Home_brassport3: Ships leave full and come back fuller. Folk out of the fog wanting passage home. I've run out of ink.
UI.Look_brassport_tides: Tide tables of the Murk, signed every day for a month. Every page says the same: NO SAILING.
UI.Look_brassport_report: An old report: 'The fishing village on the low road sank in one night when its post failed. No survivors found.' Added in pencil: 'yet.'
UI.Home_brasskids1: That's Old Hobb in my drawing. He's a giant! He climbs the tower every morning. He's deaf, too. Giants usually are.
UI.Home_brasskids2: Hobb walked the Tide road with you! I drew it. You're the small one.
UI.Home_brasskids3: Hobb rang the bells! I drew him even bigger. He doesn't fit on the paper any more.
UI.Look_brasskids_drawings: Drawings in coal: a giant old man holding a bell bigger than the tower. The tower is very small.
UI.Home_brasswarden1: Forty years I lit these roads. Look at my lanterns. Every one burned on a road that's dark now.
UI.Home_brasswarden2: When I was your age they still hung bells along the lanterways. Then the lamps came, and we thought we'd won.
UI.Home_brasswarden3: Bells back on the posts, lamps going out. My lanterns will gather dust. Good. They worked hard enough.
UI.Look_brasswarden_lanterns: A wall of old lanterns, from a tin can with a wick to a brass storm lamp. On each, a tag: the road it lit.
UI.Look_brasssunk_pipe: A cold pipe on the table, the tobacco still packed in. On the chair, a sailor's coat. The fog took him, they say, on the harbour road.
UI.Home_brasscustoms1: Every barrel of oil that passes pays the Lamp Tax. Signed by the Council. In triplicate, naturally.
UI.Home_brasscustoms2: Tax on oil, tax on wicks, tax on the tax. Between us, I don't know where it all goes. Up the Spire, I'd guess.
UI.Home_brasscustoms3: The Lamp Tax is abolished! I'm drafting the Bell Tax. Nobody is going to like it.
UI.Look_brasscustoms_taxes: Tax rolls signed by the Lamp Council. The same signature on every page, pressed harder each year.
UI.Knock_brassmouth1: A grumbling voice from inside: 'Not today. Not tomorrow either.'
UI.Knock_brassmouth2: The door is locked. The key hangs on a nail far out of reach.
UI.Home_glimclerk1: Pottle's my cousin. Yes, THAT Pottle. Has he told you about Form 12-B? He tells everyone about Form 12-B.
UI.Home_glimclerk2: Form 9-F, Disappearance of Traitors. I've filed yours. Please don't make me file it twice.
UI.Home_glimclerk3: Cousin Pottle finally abolished Form 12-B. He sent me a letter about it. Forty pages.
UI.Look_glimclerk_forms: A stack of forms waiting for a stamp. The top one: FORM 12-B, REPORT OF STOLEN GLIMMER. The stack is very tall.
UI.Home_glimglass1: I blow the globes for the lamps. The Everlamp's glass is mine. Thickest I ever made. It has to hold a sun, they said.
UI.Home_glimglass2: I made the glass of the Everlamp. If it lights, I made the thing that kills the sea. I can't sleep.
UI.Home_glimglass3: The Everlamp is dark. Today somebody asked me for a window. A plain window, to look out of. Lovely work.
UI.Look_glimglass_globes: Lamp globes cooling in rows. A tag: 'EVERLAMP, practice piece 37. Not thick enough.'
UI.Look_glimash_toys: Toys in a row on a shelf: a wooden ferry, a tin lamp, a bell with no clapper. Not a speck of dust.
UI.Look_glimash_bed: A child's bed, made tight, the cover turned down. Ready for someone, every night, for ten years.
UI.Look_glimash_desk: A letter on the desk, in a careful hand: 'Liss, I lit another road today. I will light them all until I find you.'
UI.Home_glimash1: Papa kept my room just the same. I'm twenty now. The bed is very small.
UI.Home_glimscholar1: I study the Murk. On paper, mostly; the Council keeps us out of the Vault. I copy what I can.
UI.Home_glimscholar2: The plaques said it. 'Light stills them.' I copied those words twenty years ago and never understood them. Fool.
UI.Home_glimscholar3: The Murk is a crowd! Many, each smaller than dust. I'm writing it all down. Hush came to tea. Very polite.
UI.Look_glimscholar_plaques: Copies of the Vault plaques in rows. One is circled again and again: 'Light a road, yes. Light the sea, never.'
UI.Home_glimwidow1: My husband guarded the Spire road for twenty years. He went up one night and never came down.
UI.Home_glimwidow2: Take one of his buttons. He said wickwardens were the only honest ones left. He'd want you to have it.
UI.Home_glimwidow3: I fold his uniform every morning. Then I unfold it. Then I fold it again.
UI.Home_glimwidow4: They say the sunk are walking home on the roads. I don't leave a lamp in the window any more. I ring a little bell.
UI.Look_glimwidow_uniform: A Lamp Guard's uniform, folded with great care. A button is missing.
UI.Home_glimbarracks1: Barracks. Off duty. If the sergeant asks, I'm polishing something.
UI.Home_glimbarracks2: Captain Marrow's a traitor now, they say. Don't tell anyone, but half of us cheered.
UI.Home_glimbarracks3: Sergeant Brask's bunk is still empty. He'd ring his cowbell to wake us. We hated it. I miss it.
UI.Look_glimbarracks_bunk: A neatly made bunk with a dented cowbell on the pillow. Carved in the frame: BRASK.
UI.Home_glimguild1: Lampmakers' Guild. We built the Everlamp in this very workshop. Nine years. Best work we ever did.
UI.Home_glimguild2: Nine years we built it. Nobody told us what it was for. We asked. They gave us a form.
UI.Home_glimguild3: The Guild makes bells now. Same brass, different song. The apprentices keep ringing them indoors.
UI.Look_glimguild_bench: A bench covered in brass shavings and drawings of the Everlamp. One sketch shows it with a bell hung inside. Crossed out.
UI.Knock_glimmerhold1: The curtains are drawn. Someone moves behind them, then stays very still.
UI.Knock_glimmerhold2: A sign: ENTRY BY FORM ONLY. Below it, a slot for forms. Nothing else.
UI.Home_farrowgorse1: Gorse rations everything. Look at the book: he cut every line in half when the oil stopped. Even the jam.
UI.Home_farrowgorse2: Gorse brought home a whole barrel of oil, and do you know what we did? Sat in the dark anyway. Out of habit. Then we laughed.
UI.Look_farrowgorse_rations: A ration book. Every line has been cut in half with a ruler. Then in half again.
UI.Home_farrowmother1: My boy went with the Old Man's crew, cutting wicks. He writes when he can. He hasn't written this month.
UI.Home_farrowmother2: My boy came home from the roads. He sleeps all day. Let him. He walked so far.
UI.Home_farrowmother3: He walked into the fog, they told me. I leave the door open at night. Sometimes I hear humming.
UI.Look_farrowmother_chair: A chair by the window, turned towards the road. A blanket folded on it, waiting.
UI.Home_farrowbell1: Hobb sent bells for all of us. I'm learning. Listen. ...That was a C. It was meant to be a C.
UI.Home_farrowbell2: I rang the whole Passage Song this morning! The fog came out to listen. Or to complain. Hard to say.
UI.Look_farrowbell_handbell: A brand new handbell with a tag: 'RING SOFTLY, YOU'RE NOT CALLING COWS. HOBB.'
UI.Look_farrowgone_note: A note pinned inside the door: 'Gone to join the Old Man. Back when the oil comes. Feed the cat.'
UI.Home_farrowbarn1: Empty sacks. Empty, empty, empty. We used to fill this barn to the roof. The cat's the only one eating.
UI.Home_farrowbarn2: The sacks are filling again. The cat is offended. She liked having the barn to herself.
UI.Look_farrowbarn_sacks: Empty grain sacks folded in a neat tower. A grey cat sleeps on top and does not care about you.
UI.Knock_farrow: Furious barking behind the door. A very small dog, by the sound of it. A very brave one.
UI.Home_mothnames1: I keep the names. Every sleeper who wakes, I write in the left column. Every one who stops, in the right.
UI.Home_mothnames2: Since the ringing, the left column runs off the page. I've started a second book. And a third.
UI.Look_mothnames_register: A thick register in two columns, WOKEN and STOPPED. The right column is shorter. Not short enough.
UI.Home_mothweaver1: The moths spin, I weave. The silk holds warmth the way the fog holds its sleepers.
UI.Home_mothweaver2: Take a jar of my best spinners. Open it when you're hurt. They'll keep you warm.
UI.Home_mothweaver3: Mind the loom. The moths get cross when people lean on it.
UI.Home_mothweaver4: Up-people come down to buy moth silk now. They pay in stories of the sky. I like that better than coin.
UI.Look_mothweaver_loom: A loom strung with grey silk so fine you can see through it. Moths rest on the frame, fanning slowly.
UI.Look_mothwenna_cradle: A cradle of woven silk, too small for anyone now. Carved on the rim in a child's hand: NIM. Under it, older: 'fell soft, in the thaw'.
UI.Look_mothnim_drawings: Nim's drawings: the sky, coloured blue in every one. On the last, two figures hold hands under all that blue. Underneath: 'one day'.
UI.Look_mothsleeper_cocoon: A sleeper in grey silk, breathing slow. A note pinned to the silk: 'I woke once. I liked it better here. Please let me be.'
UI.Look_mothsleeper_bells: The sleeper is still here. The note has a new line: 'Heard the bells. Very nice. Still staying.'
UI.Knock_mothgrove: A big grey moth sits on the latch and fans its wings at you. The door stays shut.
UI.Series_round: The Round Book of the Shore Watchlight.
UI.BookFound1: On the keeper's table lies a thick book: the Round Book of the Shore Watchlight. Almost every page has been torn out.
UI.BookFound2: Torn out... and carefully, one by one. Who would do that to a keepers' log?
UI.BookFound3: The first page is still here. If the others are out on the islets, I'll find them.
UI.BookAdded: The Round Book is in the menu now. Its torn pages wait in the fog.
UI.BookTable: The keeper's table. Rings of old candle wax, and a clean square where the book lay.
UI.Page_book1: The tower is finished. Tonight I lit the brazier for the first time, and out on the fog the ringers saw it and rang back: one bell, then ten. This book is for every keeper after me. Keep the flame so the ringers find their way. Keep the book so they are remembered.
UI.Page_book2: How passage is asked, as the ringers taught me. Stop at the edge. Ring three times, slow. Wait. When the fog goes firm under your foot, walk on and keep ringing. Never shout. Never run. It lets you through because you asked.
UI.Page_book3: Watched the shore all night. The fog swells at dusk and sinks before dawn, slow, like the chest of a sleeper. I timed it with the hourglass: eleven turns in, eleven out. Whatever it is, it breathes.
UI.Page_book4: Tamsin the net-mender sank in the autumn storm. At the spring ringing she walked up out of the fog on the low road, hair wet, asking for her shawl. She says she was warm. She says she slept. Nobody believes her but me.
UI.Page_book5: Riders from Glimmerhold today. A Lamp Council has been founded. 'Light is order,' they say, and they plant posts along the roads with lamps on top. Lamps are cheaper than ringers, they say. Lamps never sleep. I wonder what sleeps under them.
UI.Page_book6: Order of the Council: every bell of the roads to be tied, as a superstition. They came with rope and a form. I tied the tower bell myself so they would leave. The rope of the great bell I hid under the stair. Someone will want it one day.
UI.Page_book7: Three winters since the bells were tied. In all that time not one of the sunk has walked back up the low road. The Council says they never did. Tamsin's shawl hangs on my hook to say otherwise.
UI.Page_book8: The oil barge did not come. They say the lanterways are cheaper than towers. I let the brazier burn low. Ninth night: the last drop. I watched the fog stand up like a wall where my light used to fall. It did not come for me. It only waited.
UI.Page_book9: The post on the low road failed in the storm and nobody came to light it again. By morning the fishing village was gone, every roof of it. Forty souls. The Council sent a form. If the bells had been free, I would have rung all night.
UI.Page_book10: Oddny, keeper. The Council calls this tower closed. Closed is a word. I live here, I keep the book and I listen. A tower without light still has ears, and the fog has a great deal to say.
UI.Page_book11: Took an apprentice from Tallowby. Hesk, eleven, all elbows. On the round he stops at every post and puts his ear to the fog. The other boys laughed at him. I didn't. He'll make a wickwarden, or a ringer. Maybe both. - Oddny
UI.Page_book12: First round alone. Lit the Spur, the shore lamps, the long causeway. Master Oddny says I'm too slow. She's right. I stopped at every post to listen. The fog is not silent. Why does nobody say so? - H.
UI.Page_book13: Put my ear to the fog by a dead lamp. It hums: a low note, steady, like a big animal asleep. When I lit the lamp the hum stopped, like a held breath. I wonder if light hurts it. - H.
UI.Page_book14: Went down into the Lamp Vault with a candle and a pass I wrote myself. The first keepers put it in brass: 'Light stills them. Stilled, they bear our weight. Stilled too long, they do not wake.' The Council keeps those plaques locked. Now I know why. - Oddny
UI.Page_book15: Councillor Ashgrave brought his daughter on his rounds. Liss, six, with a pocket lantern bigger than her hand. She sat at the edge of the road and sang to the fog, and the fog hummed back. Ash laughed. I didn't. I think it liked her. - H.
UI.Page_book16: Liss walked out on the Spire road to sing to someone crying under it. The post there was new, and the fog was frightened of it. She sank. I begged them to let me ring. The Council forbade it. Ash lit every lamp on that road instead, all night. I still hear the bell I didn't ring. - H.
UI.Page_book17: My last entry. My hands shake too much for the brazier now. The book goes to Hesk. Boy, the Council will tell you the fog is nothing. Keep listening anyway. And if you can't ring, at least don't let them light the whole sea. - Oddny
UI.Page_book18: A mother came to the tower in the night. Her little one had wandered onto a dark road. I went out and listened. Under the road, far down, something small was laughing. I couldn't tell her. Who would believe it? - H.
UI.Page_book19: I understand now. The fog does not eat the sunk. It holds them, asleep and warm, the way a hen holds her eggs, and waits for someone to ring for them. Nobody rings. So they sleep, and sleep. - H.
UI.Page_book20: Ash spoke to the Council: a lamp on the Spire to light the whole Murk at once and make it stone forever. 'No more sinking.' No more sleepers either; every one of them would stop. He has never once listened to the fog. - H.
UI.Page_book21: Cut my first wick tonight, on the barge road to Glimmerhold. Every barrel that doesn't reach the Spire is a day the sleepers keep. Gorse's people are starving; we'll share what we take. Let them call me a thief. I've been called worse by better. - H.
UI.Page_book22: The farmers call me the Old Man now. I taught them to walk the bare fog, to ask and not to take. We cut wicks, never people. Every night I ring where I can. Every night it isn't enough. - H.
UI.Page_book23: The Council's inspectors come tomorrow to burn every keepers' book. I am tearing out the pages that tell the truth and hiding them in the fog, by the lamps, where only someone who lights them will look. Forgive me, keepers. It's the only way your words survive. - H.
UI.Page_book24: If you are reading this, you lit the Shore tower again and walked the islets for these pages. Then you listened. Good. The fog is not our enemy; it never was. Ring for the sleepers. Stop the lamp on the Spire. And forgive an old man who lied to keep them warm. - H.

UI.ItemDesc_irontonic: Tastes of nails. Raises one ally's defence for a while.
UI.ItemDesc_quickstep: Very strong tea. Raises one ally's speed for a while.
UI.ItemDesc_pepperpouch: Thrown in the face. Blinds one enemy.
UI.ItemDesc_sootbomb: A puff of choking black. Gives one enemy Soot.

UI.ItemDesc_rustdust: Eats at armour. Lowers one enemy's defence.

UI.ItemDesc_fogwhistle: Its note bends the fog. Escape from a battle.
UI.ItemDesc_tinpole: An apprentice's pole. Light, honest, a little bent.
UI.ItemDesc_brasspole: A proper wickwarden's pole with a brass hook.
UI.ItemDesc_lamphook: Long reach, heavy head. Wicks and skulls beware.
UI.ItemDesc_gildedpole: A Council pole, gilt and balanced.
UI.ItemDesc_dawnstaff: The pole of the first wickwarden. It glows at both ends.
UI.ItemDesc_ladle: For stew, and for people who complain about the stew.
UI.ItemDesc_skillet: Bram's pan. Nineteen years of seasoning. Back a bit oilier.
UI.ItemDesc_cleaver: A serious knife for serious onions.
UI.ItemDesc_copperpot: Hits like a bell. Bram swears it's for cooking.
UI.ItemDesc_grandmapan: The heaviest pan ever forged. Also, the best.
UI.ItemDesc_brassdividers: A surveyor's compass with needle points.
UI.ItemDesc_fogcalipers: Measures the thickness of fog, and of enemies.
UI.ItemDesc_starcompass: Points at the stars, and through armour.
UI.ItemDesc_meridian: Twin needles that never miss their mark.
UI.ItemDesc_guardlantern: A Lamp Guard's lantern-mace. Heavy, bright, rude.
UI.ItemDesc_ironlantern: An old vault lantern. Its cage is a weapon in itself.
UI.ItemDesc_beacon: The great lantern of the old Guard captains.
UI.ItemDesc_bronzebell: Hobb's own bell. Rings true, hits hard.
UI.ItemDesc_stormbell: A ship's bell rescued from the tower. Very loud.
UI.ItemDesc_passagebell: The bell that rings the Passage Song.
UI.ItemDesc_paleshard: A sliver of the Murk itself, cool to the touch.
UI.ItemDesc_greyshard: A heavier sliver of the Murk.
UI.ItemDesc_duskshard: A sliver of fog from the deepest dusk.
UI.ItemDesc_murkheart: A shard that beats, slowly, like a sleeper's heart.
UI.ItemDesc_silknet: A moth-catcher's net of grey silk.
UI.ItemDesc_moonnet: Woven under moth light. Light and quick.
UI.ItemDesc_thousandnet: Every moth of the grove helped weave it.
UI.ItemDesc_patchcoat: Pell's old coat. More patch than coat.
UI.ItemDesc_oilskin: Keeps out fog, rain and most beaks. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_surveyorcoat: Many pockets, every one with a pencil in it.
UI.ItemDesc_greatcoat: Long and heavy, with a collar for bad weather. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_mothcloak: Woven by moths. Light as dusk. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_dawncoat: A coat the colour of the hour before sunrise. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_leatherapron: Thick enough to stop a cleaver. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_banquetapron: Worn at the greatest feast of the age. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_guardmail: The plate of the Lamp Guard.
UI.ItemDesc_wardenplate: Heavy plate for the captains of the roads. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_beaconplate: Old armour that glows faintly in the dark. Halves flame.
UI.ItemDesc_belfryrobe: Dusty, warm, smells of rope. Halves sound.
UI.ItemDesc_fogweave: Woven by the moth-folk from fog that was willing. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_tollrobe: Worn by the ringers of old for the great tolls. Halves sound.
UI.ItemDesc_murkmantle: The Murk's own grey, offered as a gift. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_candlestub: A lucky stub of candle. Raises HP.
UI.ItemDesc_luckypenny: Given back by the Tide road's current. Raises speed.
UI.ItemDesc_brassbutton: A Guard's button, very sturdy. Raises defence.
UI.ItemDesc_mothwing: Raises speed and keeps sleep away.
UI.ItemDesc_eartrumpet: Hobb's spare. Raises resistance. Halves sound.
UI.ItemDesc_wardbell: A tiny bell that keeps you awake.
UI.ItemDesc_clearlens: Keeps the eyes clear of Blind. Raises attack a little.
UI.ItemDesc_emberring: A ring still warm from a forge. Raises attack.
UI.ItemDesc_pocketsun: A marble full of light. Raises magic and WICK.
UI.ItemDesc_handbell: Hobb's gift. 'Won't save you. Might help.'
UI.ItemDesc_heartwick: The first flame. It never cools.
UI.ItemDesc_passagescore: The old score of the Passage Song.
UI.ItemDesc_form12b: Report of Stolen Glimmer, blank. In triplicate.
UI.ItemDesc_chart: The currents of the Murk, drawn in green ink.
UI.ItemDesc_emberhook: A lamp hook left in the forge. Strikes with flame.
UI.ItemDesc_searskillet: Always hot, somehow. Strikes with flame.
UI.ItemDesc_fogneedle: A needle that stitches fog. Strikes with murk.
UI.ItemDesc_belllantern: A guard lantern with a clapper. Strikes with sound.
UI.ItemDesc_hollowshard: A shard that sings when struck. Strikes with sound.
UI.ItemDesc_dozenet: The moths in it yawn. May cause sleep.
UI.ItemDesc_crackedbell: Out of tune, and loud. May stun.
UI.ItemDesc_murkpearl: A pearl from the Maw. Guards against blind.
UI.ItemDesc_oldwick: Hesk's wick, cut short. Raises WICK and magic.
UI.ItemDesc_greenclapper: Gnawed but sound. Guards against stun.
UI.ItemDesc_sergeantbadge: Brask's badge. Raises attack and defence.
UI.ItemDesc_ashcrown: The Council's chain, melted down. Raises everything.
UI.ItemDesc_charcoallocket: Keeps the lungs clean. Guards against soot.
UI.ItemDesc_sparktin: Crackles with every blow. More BRIGHT per hit.
UI.ItemDesc_litmatch: Catches even in fog. Starts battles with some BRIGHT.
UI.ItemDesc_mothlantern: Caged glowmoths. Regain HP at the start of battle.
UI.ItemDesc_earlybell: Pell's alarm bell. Acts sooner in battle.
UI.ItemDesc_belltonic: Raises an ally's magic for a while.
UI.ItemDesc_veilash: Veils the party for a while.
UI.ItemDesc_mothjar: The party regains HP every turn.
UI.ItemDesc_dawnember: Revives an ally with full HP.
UI.ItemDesc_ringerplate: An old guard's plate with a bell on the shoulder. Halves sound.
UI.ItemDesc_harbourapron: Harbour-kitchen cloth. Smells of fish and victory. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_firstwick: The first wickwarden's wick, still oily after all these years. Flame.
UI.ItemDesc_drownedladle: The drowned village's last ladle. Hits can lower defence.
UI.ItemDesc_lisslantern: A child's dented lantern. Raises WICK, magic. Stops blindness.
UI.ItemDesc_ferryapron: Tarred canvas, a ferryman's for forty years. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_olddividers: Used to chart the islets before the lanterways. Murk.
UI.ItemDesc_farrowbrooch: A tin wheatsheaf of hopeful farmers. Raises attack, defence.

UI.ItemDesc_nightlantern: A Tideway tower guard's lantern, heavy as a promise. Flame.
UI.ItemDesc_mapmakercoat: Pockets for pencils, pockets for pockets. Halves murk.
UI.ItemDesc_ferryshard: A piece of the boat the fog kept, humming softly. Murk.
UI.ItemDesc_shorenet: Knotted on the shoals by gentle hands. Hits can put to sleep.
UI.ItemDesc_ferryoar: A carved oar charm. Raises speed. Battles start with BRIGHT.
